---
title: "Session 8 · Visualization"
subtitle: "Base graphics, ggplot2, and honest statistical communication"
---

## Learning goals

Choose a plot for a statistical question, construct and annotate base R plots,
read and build layered ggplot2 code, and export a figure at an explicit size.
Use the optional geom catalogue to find less familiar drawing methods.

## Materials

- [Slides](slides.qmd)
- <a href="slides.html#/geom-catalogue">Complete ggplot2 geom catalogue in the slides</a>
- [Guided lab](lab.qmd)
- Lab starter—choose one: `starter/visualization-lab.Rmd` or `starter/visualization-lab.qmd`

Either base graphics or ggplot2 may be used where both support the communication
goal. The lab asks for one figure in each style so that you can read both.

## Lesson sequence

After the base R examples, we build a first ggplot, choose displays for
distributions and comparisons, add summaries and uncertainty, and show repeated
visits. The final blocks refine scales, critique the figure, and export it.
The optional geom catalogue includes representative figures alongside its lists.
